source.anchor: §4.1.1 Eq. (14)–(15) and the adjacent component and joint coefficient laws; implicit uncut finite-sum consequence
source.original_text: Attributed reconstruction of an implicit finite-sum consequence of Eq. (14)–(15) and adjacent laws, not a standalone printed theorem. In the unconditioned joint standard Gaussian coefficient model, for fixed level i and deterministic unit trailing vectors, sum the actual terms sqrt(n) a_i,p <Xi_i,p, psi_i^tensor p> over all even 4<=p<=P. The sum is Gaussian with mean zero and variance n times sum_p a_i,p^2. Here P=2^(64(h+1)), K=2^(74(h+1)), S_i=sum_{j=0}^{h-i}K^j, a_i,p=1/[p^4 S_i^2 sqrt((h-i+1) log(2 P S_i))], and psi_i repeats the j-th trailing unit vector K^j times. Xi_i,p is the actual ordered block with n^(p S_i) coordinates. The source prescribes sufficiently large n and its depth, and radial and conditional laws are separate.

let g := fun (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1))
    (p : {p : ℕ // Even p ∧ 4 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 ^ (64 * (h + 1))})
    (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val))
    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ
      ((Fin p.val × (Σ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1),
        Fin ((2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val))) → Fin n.val)) ↦
  let S : ℕ := ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
  let a : ℝ := 1 / ((p.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S : ℝ) ^ 2 *
    Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S)))
  Real.sqrt n.val * a * ∑ c, ξ c * ∏ s, u s.2.1 (c s)
;
∀ (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1))
    (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val))
    (_hu : ∀ j, ‖u j‖ = 1),
    let P := {p : Fin (2 ^ (64 * (h + 1)) + 1) // Even p.val ∧ 4 ≤ p.val}
    let B := Fin (h + 1) × P
    let C := fun b : B ↦
      ((Fin b.2.val.val × (Σ j : Fin (h - b.1.val + 1),
        Fin ((2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val))) → Fin n.val)
    let degree := fun p : P ↦
      (⟨p.val.val, p.property.1, p.property.2, Nat.le_of_lt_succ p.val.isLt⟩ :
        {p : ℕ // Even p ∧ 4 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 ^ (64 * (h + 1))})
    let S : ℕ := ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
    let a := fun p : P ↦ 1 / ((p.val.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S : ℝ) ^ 2 *
      Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S)))
    let F := fun (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Σ b : B, C b)) ↦ ∑ p : P,
      g n h i (degree p) u
        (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun c : C (i, p) ↦ ξ ⟨(i, p), c⟩))
    HasLaw F (gaussianReal 0 (((n.val : ℝ) * ∑ p : P, (a p) ^ 2).toNNReal))
      (stdGaussian (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Σ b : B, C b)))

blind_reconstruction.text:
Fix a positive integer n, a nonnegative integer h, and an integer i with 0 <= i <= h. Write [d] = {0, ..., d-1}, set K = 2^(64(h+1)) and M = 2^(74(h+1)), and let P be the set of even integers p with 4 <= p <= K. For every k in [h+1] let m_k = h-k+1, and for p in P let T_(k,p) consist of the triples (r,j,l) with r in [p], j in [m_k], and l in [M^j]. Let C_(k,p) be the set of all functions from T_(k,p) to [n]. Take a standard Gaussian vector Xi in the real Euclidean space with coordinates (k,p,c), where k is in [h+1], p is in P, and c is in C_(k,p). Thus all entries Xi_(k,p,c) are independent standard normal variables.

Fix any deterministic family (u_j)_(j in [m_i]) of vectors in R^[n] with ||u_j||_2 = 1 for each j. Set S = sum_(j in [m_i]) M^j and, for p in P, set
a(p) = 1 / (p^4 S^2 sqrt(m_i log(2 K S))),
where log denotes the natural logarithm. Define the real-valued map
F(Xi) = sqrt(n) sum_(p in P) a(p) sum_(c in C_(i,p)) Xi_(i,p,c) prod_((r,j,l) in T_(i,p)) u_j(c(r,j,l)).

Then F is almost everywhere measurable under the standard Gaussian coefficient law, and its pushforward law is the real Gaussian with mean 0 and variance n sum_(p in P) a(p)^2. The nonnegative conversion on the variance leaves this expression unchanged. The assertion is for each fixed i and fixed unit-vector family; it gives no simultaneous bound over vector families and no law for a family chosen as a function of Xi. It does not assert that two evaluations using the same coefficient array are independent.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SlcLsiQueryComplexity.AngularDegree
import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SlcLsiQueryComplexity.CoefficientBlocks
import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.HasGaussianLaw.Independence

/-!
# Gaussian law of a fixed-level angular degree sum

Zhou–Suzuki, arXiv:2611.05813v1 (CC BY 4.0), §4.1.1, Eq. (14)–(15).
At fixed deterministic unit directions, the literal angular polynomial has a
centered Gaussian law with variance `n * ∑ p, aᵢₚ²`. This expands an implicit
finite-sum consequence of the paper's adjacent one-block and joint laws.
No radial, adaptive, or conditional law is asserted.
-/

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped BigOperators

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SlcLsiQueryComplexity.AngularDegreeSum

open AngularDegree CoefficientBlocks

/-- The actual fixed-level degree sum under the unconditioned coefficient law.
Independence and second moments come from the existing block laws, not premises. -/
theorem angularDegreeSum_hasLaw (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1))
    (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val))
    (hu : ∀ j, ‖u j‖ = 1) :
    let P := {p : Fin (2 ^ (64 * (h + 1)) + 1) // Even p.val ∧ 4 ≤ p.val}
    let B := Fin (h + 1) × P
    let C := fun b : B ↦
      ((Fin b.2.val.val × (Σ j : Fin (h - b.1.val + 1),
        Fin ((2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val))) → Fin n.val)
    let degree := fun p : P ↦
      (⟨p.val.val, p.property.1, p.property.2, Nat.le_of_lt_succ p.val.isLt⟩ :
        {p : ℕ // Even p ∧ 4 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 ^ (64 * (h + 1))})
    let S : ℕ := ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
    let a := fun p : P ↦ 1 / ((p.val.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S : ℝ) ^ 2 *
      Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S)))
    let F := fun (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Σ b : B, C b)) ↦ ∑ p : P,
      angularDegreeComponent n h i (degree p) u
        (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun c : C (i, p) ↦ ξ ⟨(i, p), c⟩))
    HasLaw F (gaussianReal 0 (((n.val : ℝ) * ∑ p : P, (a p) ^ 2).toNNReal))
      (stdGaussian (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Σ b : B, C b))) := by
  intro P B C degree S a F
  classical
  let Ω := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Σ b : B, C b)
  let μ : Measure Ω := stdGaussian Ω
  let ν := fun b : B ↦ stdGaussian (EuclideanSpace ℝ (C b))
  let blocks := fun (ξ : Ω) (b : B) ↦
    (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun c : C b ↦ ξ ⟨b, c⟩) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (C b))
  let atLevel : P → B := fun p ↦ (i, p)
  let component (p : P) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (C (atLevel p)) → ℝ :=
    angularDegreeComponent n h i (degree p) u
  let X (p : P) (ξ : Ω) : ℝ := component p (blocks ξ (atLevel p))
  have hJoint : HasLaw blocks (Measure.pi ν) μ := jointCoefficientBlocks_hasLaw n h
  have hBlock (b : B) : HasLaw (fun ξ ↦ blocks ξ b) (ν b) μ := by
    have hEval := measurePreserving_eval (μ := ν) b
    have h := hEval.fun_comp_hasLaw hJoint
    exact h
  have hIndep : iIndepFun (fun b ξ ↦ blocks ξ b) μ :=
    (iIndepFun_iff_hasLaw_pi_pi hBlock).2 hJoint
  have hInjective : Function.Injective atLevel := fun _ _ h ↦ congrArg Prod.snd h
  have hComponent (p : P) :
      HasLaw (component p) (gaussianReal 0 (((n.val : ℝ) * (a p) ^ 2).toNNReal))
        (ν (atLevel p)) := angularDegreeComponent_hasLaw n h i (degree p) u hu
  have hX (p : P) :
      HasLaw (X p) (gaussianReal 0 (((n.val : ℝ) * (a p) ^ 2).toNNReal)) μ :=
    (hComponent p).fun_comp (hBlock (atLevel p))
  have hXIndep : iIndepFun X μ :=
    (hIndep.precomp hInjective).comp₀ component
      (fun p ↦ (hBlock (atLevel p)).aemeasurable)
      (fun p ↦ (hBlock (atLevel p)).map_eq.symm ▸ (hComponent p).aemeasurable)
  have hGaussian (p : P) : HasGaussianLaw (X p) μ := (hX p).hasGaussianLaw
  have hSum : HasGaussianLaw F μ := hXIndep.hasGaussianLaw_fun_sum hGaussian
  have hMean : ∫ ξ, F ξ ∂μ = 0 := by
    change (∫ ξ, ∑ p : P, X p ξ ∂μ) = 0
    rw [integral_finsetSum _ (fun p _ ↦ (hGaussian p).integrable)]
    simp only [fun p ↦ (hX p).integral_eq, integral_id_gaussianReal, Finset.sum_const_zero]
  have hVar : Var[F; μ] = (n.val : ℝ) * ∑ p : P, (a p) ^ 2 := by
    have hPointwise : F = ∑ p : P, X p := by
      funext ξ
      change (∑ p : P, X p ξ) = (∑ p : P, X p) ξ
      exact (Finset.sum_apply ξ Finset.univ X).symm
    rw [hPointwise]
    rw [IndepFun.variance_sum (X := X) (s := Finset.univ)
      (fun p _ ↦ (hGaussian p).memLp_two)
      (fun p _ q _ hpq ↦ hXIndep.indepFun hpq), Finset.mul_sum]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p _ ↦ ?_
    rw [(hX p).variance_eq, variance_id_gaussianReal]
    exact Real.coe_toNNReal _ (mul_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg n.val) (sq_nonneg (a p)))
  change HasLaw F (gaussianReal 0 (((n.val : ℝ) * ∑ p : P, (a p) ^ 2).toNNReal)) μ
  exact ⟨hSum.aemeasurable, by rw [hSum.map_eq_gaussianReal, hMean, hVar]⟩

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SlcLsiQueryComplexity.AngularDegreeSum

candidate_publication_context.statement: Fix a level i and deterministic unit vectors u_i,…,u_h. Let the tensor coefficients at all levels and allowed degrees have their unconditioned joint standard Gaussian law. The actual angular polynomial at level i, obtained by summing its degree components at those directions, is centered Gaussian with variance n times the sum of the squared source amplitudes.

formulae.label: Source degrees and amplitudes
formulae.tex: K=2^{74(h+1)},\quad P=2^{64(h+1)},\quad \mathcal P=\{4,6,\ldots,P\},\quad S_i=\sum_{j=0}^{h-i}K^j,\qquad a_{i,p}=\frac{1}{p^4 S_i^2\sqrt{(h-i+1)\log(2PS_i)}}.

formulae.label: Exact uncut angular law
formulae.tex: \begin{gathered}\psi_i=u_i\otimes u_{i+1}^{\otimes K}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_h^{\otimes K^{h-i}},\\ F_i^\Xi(u)=\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\sqrt n\,a_{i,p}\langle\Xi_{i,p},\psi_i^{\otimes p}\rangle,\\ \Xi\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{\mathcal G_n})\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F_i^\Xi(u)\sim\mathcal N\!\left(0,n\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}a_{i,p}^2\right).\end{gathered}

assumptions: The dimension n is a positive integer, h is a natural depth, and 0≤i≤h. The paper fixes h from sufficiently large n; the isolated identity does not use that relation and does not enlarge the admissible hard family.
The trailing directions u_j are deterministic and satisfy ‖u_j‖₂=1. The source uses the even degree set from 4 through P; repetitions in the ordered tensor are kept.

The randomness is the unconditioned standard Gaussian on the full Euclidean coefficient direct sum, with the product of block laws derived from the existing coefficient theorem. The spatial input and any adaptive or conditioned coefficient laws are not involved.

lesson.statement: Fix a level i and deterministic unit vectors u_i,…,u_h. Let the tensor coefficients at all levels and allowed degrees have their unconditioned joint standard Gaussian law. The actual angular polynomial at level i, obtained by summing its degree components at those directions, is centered Gaussian with variance n times the sum of the squared source amplitudes.
lesson.formula: \begin{gathered}\psi_i=u_i\otimes u_{i+1}^{\otimes K}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_h^{\otimes K^{h-i}},\\ F_i^\Xi(u)=\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\sqrt n\,a_{i,p}\langle\Xi_{i,p},\psi_i^{\otimes p}\rangle,\\ \Xi\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{\mathcal G_n})\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F_i^\Xi(u)\sim\mathcal N\!\left(0,n\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}a_{i,p}^2\right).\end{gathered}
lesson.reader_note: The point of the calculation is that tensor degree changes the amplitude and the coefficient block, but does not prevent Gaussian addition at a fixed input. The source later uses the variance notation v_i for the squared-amplitude sum. Its actual H_i also contains a radial factor and needs a separate zero-block convention.

steps.title: Use the right coefficient block for each degree
steps.text: Project the full coefficient draw to its ordered blocks. The joint law is a product, so evaluation at a block gives its standard Gaussian marginal. Distinct degrees at a fixed level select distinct blocks. Apply the deterministic tensor polynomial in each block; the unit directions give the exact component variance.
steps.lean: The joint coefficient law is used to recover the block marginals, then the exact AngularDegree law is composed with the projection via HasLaw.fun_comp.

steps.title: Preserve independence under fixed evaluations
steps.text: For any finite collection of degree labels, the inverse image of a product event for the scalar values is a product event in those different coefficient blocks. Hence their probabilities factor. This argument fixes the directions before drawing the coefficients and is not valid just from the pointwise law if the directions depend on the draw.
steps.formula: \mathbb P\{X_p\in A_p\text{ for all }p\in\mathcal P\}=\prod_{p\in\mathcal P}\mathbb P\{X_p\in A_p\}.
steps.lean: Recover mutual independence from the joint product law, restrict along the injective map p↦(i,p), and compose with the component maps. Their laws provide the needed almost-everywhere measurability.

steps.title: Add Gaussian means and variances
steps.text: A finite sum of independent Gaussian variables is Gaussian. The component laws give finite second moments, hence integrability; add their zero means. Independence makes the mixed covariance terms vanish, leaving the sum of the component variances. The resulting Gaussian is determined by that mean and variance.
steps.formula: \begin{aligned}\mathbb E F_i^\Xi(u)&=\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E X_p=0,\\ \operatorname{Var}(F_i^\Xi(u))&=\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\operatorname{Var}(X_p)=n\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}a_{i,p}^2.\end{aligned}
steps.lean: Mathlib's independent Gaussian finite-sum theorem supplies Gaussianity. integral_finsetSum and IndepFun.variance_sum calculate its parameters; map_eq_gaussianReal then identifies the exact law.

lesson.lean_statement: HasLaw packages almost-everywhere measurability and equality of the pushforward to the displayed centered normal. The finite-subtype degree adapter retains the same natural degree and adds no assumption.
lesson.lean_proof: Read the proof as actual coefficient projections → independent scalar Gaussian values → exact finite-sum law. The variance parameter uses toNNReal only to encode nonnegativity; it does not approximate the variance.
lesson.dependency_notes: Two genuine source-model laws are reused from Samplinglib. Mathlib supplies the generic product and Gaussian-sum facts. The fixed-input radial field needed before Eq. (51) is a future consumer, not an already compiled edge.
